analysis.title: US Rates Tail Risk: A Republican Sweep
key_insights: The tail risk from the US midterm elections is a Republican sweep (House and Senate), which could lead to higher government spending. Markets are positioned for divided government and fiscal gridlock, so a sweep removes the expected fiscal brake and risks a long-end selloff.
Polymarket odds cited: Republican sweep 5%, Democratic sweep 73%, Democratic House with Republican Senate 23% (25% in the summary section), Republican House with Democratic Senate 1%.

Preferred expression is a 3m USD payer switch: long 30y payers relative to 5y payers, strikes around ATM +25bp on each underlying as a starting point. Exact strikes, notionals, premium and delta/vega balance are to be set from the live vol and skew surface.

Transmission channel: Republican sweep, expected gridlock fails to arrive, more scope for fiscal measures, higher deficit and issuance expectations, higher long-end term premium, 30y underperforming 5y. Unified control creates capacity for policy change but does not guarantee fiscal expansion.

The author prefers the option switch over a large linear steepener because the sweep probability is low. The aim is to benefit from disproportionate long-end weakness while choosing how much premium and short-leg risk to take.

A payer switch is not automatically limited-loss. If 30y payers are financed by selling 5y payers, the short leg can lose material amounts, including when the curve thesis disappoints. DV01 matching alone does not balance vega, gamma or convexity.

3m expiry is chosen over 1m. A 1m expiry concentrates on the immediate election reaction, while 3m gives the fiscal thesis time to feed through deficit expectations, Treasury supply, term premium and the curve, at the cost of more premium.

Desk observation (historical colour, not a current quote): 5y skew was offered while 30y had not repriced to the same extent. Further cheapening of the short 5y leg relative to the long 30y leg would help the mark, but an already cheap 5y leg may make the financing less attractive.

Republican House / Republican Senate: expect 5s30s bear steepening. Cash: buy 5y UST / sell 30y UST, DV01 weighted. Swaps: receive fixed 5y SOFR / pay fixed 30y SOFR. A Treasury-supply variant is sell 30y UST / receive fixed 30y SOFR, DV01 matched, targeting a narrower or more negative swap spread.

Democratic House / Republican Senate: gridlock arrives, 5s30s bull flattening. Cash: sell 5y UST / buy 30y UST, DV01 weighted. Swaps: pay fixed 5y SOFR / receive fixed 30y SOFR. Risk is that the outcome is already discounted, and there may be renewed volatility later around budgets, shutdowns or debt-limit talks.

Democratic House / Democratic Senate: stronger congressional brake and a possible check on future Fed appointments, favouring flattening with a firm front end. Expression: sell 5y / buy 30y UST, or pay 5y / receive 30y SOFR. Kevin Warsh was confirmed as Fed Chair on May 13 by 54-45.

Republican House / Democratic Senate (1%): divided government, so a fiscal brake exists. The author has less conviction in a directional trade and would not force a cash-curve or swap-spread position. Forward-rate or policy-sensitive volatility could be examined if priced attractively.
Results arrive overnight into Wednesday morning after Tuesday's vote, and a definitive outcome may take longer. The note is a scenario framework, not an election forecast.

trade_ideas.description: Long 30y USD payer swaptions versus 5y payer swaptions (payer switch), 3m expiry, strikes around ATM +25bp on each underlying
trade_ideas.rationale: A Republican sweep removes the expected fiscal brake and could raise long-end term premium, with 30y underperforming 5y.
trade_ideas.risk: Sweep may not happen or may change little. A growth or inflation shock could reprice 5y as much as 30y. Relative skew can move against the package, and the short 5y payer leg can lose material amounts.

trade_ideas.description: 5s30s steepener in a Republican sweep: buy 5y UST / sell 30y UST DV01 weighted, or receive fixed 5y SOFR / pay fixed 30y SOFR
trade_ideas.rationale: Gridlock fails to arrive and long-end term premium rises.
trade_ideas.risk: Unified government may not produce enough fiscal change, or the market may price the shock through the belly and Fed expectations.

trade_ideas.description: Sell 30y UST / receive fixed 30y SOFR, DV01 matched, for Treasury cheapening versus swaps (narrower or more negative swap spread)
trade_ideas.rationale: A Treasury-specific supply interpretation of a Republican sweep.
trade_ideas.risk: A distinct basis exposure with funding and balance-sheet drivers as well as fiscal risk.

trade_ideas.description: 5s30s bull flattener if Democratic House / Republican Senate: sell 5y UST / buy 30y UST DV01 weighted, or pay fixed 5y SOFR / receive fixed 30y SOFR
trade_ideas.rationale: Gridlock reduces scope for additional deficit expansion, so some long-end premium comes out.
trade_ideas.risk: The outcome is already sufficiently discounted and the incremental reaction is small.

trade_ideas.description: 5s30s flattener if Democratic House / Democratic Senate: sell 5y / buy 30y UST, or pay 5y / receive 30y SOFR, DV01 weighted
trade_ideas.rationale: A stronger institutional check could lower long-end premium, and a Fed seen as insulated keeps the front end firm.
trade_ideas.risk: Congressional constraint leaves existing deficits, issuance and inflation pressures largely intact.

risk_factors: A Republican sweep may not happen or may produce little change in expected policy.
A growth or inflation shock could reprice Fed expectations through 5y as strongly as the long end, so an outright short-duration trade works while the steepener disappoints.
Relative skew can move against the payer switch, and time decay and premium matter.
An ATM +25bp structure may not pay off if the sell-off is too small.
The short 5y payer leg can generate material losses, including when the curve thesis disappoints.
A Democratic House and Republican Senate outcome may already be discounted, leaving little tradable movement.
Gridlock may bring renewed volatility around budgets, shutdowns or debt-limit negotiations.
The final election result may take longer than overnight into Wednesday.
vol_and_positioning: Markets are positioned for divided government and fiscal gridlock, so a Republican sweep would be a positioning surprise for the long end.
Desk observation: 5y skew was offered while 30y skew had not repriced to the same extent. This is historical colour, not a current quote.
Payer switch: long 30y payers versus 5y payers, 3m expiry, around ATM +25bp on each leg. Relative skew can move against the package, and time decay and premium matter.
A payer switch does not balance vega, gamma or convexity through DV01 matching alone, and the short 5y payer leg can lose material amounts.
In the Republican House / Democratic Senate case, forward-rate or policy-sensitive volatility could be worth examining, but uncertainty alone does not make long vol attractive.

tension_points.bull_case: A Republican sweep removes the expected fiscal brake, which could raise deficit and issuance expectations and push long-end term premium higher, so 30y underperforms 5y and the payer switch gains.
tension_points.bear_case: Unified control creates capacity for policy change but does not guarantee fiscal expansion. The sweep may produce little change, or a growth or inflation shock may reprice the front end as much as the long end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Republican sweep that does not lead the market to infer a more expansionary fiscal path than it had priced, or a 30y payer sell-off too small to carry the ATM +25bp structure through expiry.

theme_stances.key_argument: If the expected shift towards gridlock fails to arrive, the long end is where the clearest repricing would occur.
theme_stances.evidence: Markets are positioned for divided government and fiscal gridlock
